clue.text: Feathers going the other way

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the soft fine plumage of young birds, used to fill pillows
second meaning: heading in the direction opposite to up

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests ruffled plumage; really it is two separate senses of one short word, a noun and an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the fluffy under-plumage of birds and the direction opposite to upward.

clue.text: Don Draper at first supports Delaware lobster, for instance

parts.note: DE is the postal abbreviation for Delaware
a capo is a Mafia boss, a don

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: the first letter of Draper

explanation.surface: Don Draper of Mad Men propping up a Delaware seafood business.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, what supports another word sits below it. 'Don Draper' looks like the Mad Men character, but it splits into a Mafia boss and a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Decapods are crustaceans with ten legs, and lobsters are a standard example of the order.

clue.text: Dispense with a view erroneously

indicators.note: something done erroneously comes out wrong, so the letters land in the wrong order

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Mistakenly abandoning an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To waive a right or requirement is to forgo it, setting it aside.

clue.text: Political cartoonist admitting pointer to Canada's leader is not disseminated very widely

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the cartoonist's name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Thomas Nast, the 19th-century American political cartoonist
an arrow points the way

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the country is kept

parts.note: the leader of Canada is its first letter

explanation.surface: A political cartoonist sneaks in a jab at Canada's leader, but the drawing barely circulates.
explanation.walkthrough: NAST holds ARROW and C. To narrowcast is to broadcast to a small, targeted audience; the past participle has the same form.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrowcast material is transmitted only to a limited, specialised audience, the opposite of a broadcast.

clue.text: Topless sailor's cry: "West, you betcha!"

indicators.note: without a top means the first letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: Land ho! is the lookout's cry on sighting land
W is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A shirtless sailor shouts about heading west, adding an enthusiastic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' looks like a state of undress, but it removes the L from LAND HO.
explanation.definitionFit: 'And how!' is an American exclamation of emphatic agreement, like 'you bet'.

clue.text: Santorum joins playwright in a no-emissions vehicle

parts.note: Rick Santorum, US senator and presidential candidate
George Bernard Shaw, Irish dramatist

explanation.surface: A conservative politician and a dramatist share an environmentally clean ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joins' simply puts the two names side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is pulled by a person on foot or bicycle, so it burns no fuel and gives off no exhaust.

clue.text: Woman in black adopts no Russian or French façade

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the woman's word takes a letter inside it

parts.note: a widow traditionally wears black mourning
N is a short form of no
Russian and French are both salad dressings

explanation.surface: A woman in mourning refuses both Russian and French and puts on a brave face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian or French' looks like languages or nationalities, but they are kinds of salad dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Window dressing is a misleadingly attractive presentation that hides the real state of things.

clue.text: In the midst of a frolic, some primates might be like this clue (when you read it aloud)

definitions.text: like this clue (when you read it aloud)

indicators.note: in the midst of means inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: an antic is a playful caper
apes are one group of primates

explanation.surface: Mid-romp, a few monkeys behave rather like this very clue.
explanation.walkthrough: An anapest is a metrical foot of two light syllables then a stressed one; spoken, the clue falls into that da-da-DUM rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Anapestic verse uses feet of two unstressed syllables followed by a stressed one, the rhythm the clue itself has.

clue.text: Party ran NYC sector as a dictatorship

indicators.note: a sector is one part of a larger whole, so the answer is a part of the words before it

parts.note: read straight through the end of Party, all of ran and the start of NYC

explanation.surface: A political party ran part of New York City like a dictatorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like a political party, as in Tammany Hall, but only its last letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyranny is cruel, absolute rule by one person, the essence of a dictatorship.

clue.text: Traitor who is a newspaper writer about liquor?

parts.note: a fifth is a US bottle of spirits holding a fifth of a gallon
a writer of a regular newspaper column

explanation.surface: A turncoat who happens to be a journalist writing about booze.
explanation.walkthrough: A columnist writing about a fifth is a fifth columnist; 'about' gives the subject, and the question mark flags the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fifth column is a group secretly working for the enemy from within, so a member of it is a traitor.

clue.text: Commercial for spicy dish produces one thousand

parts.note: chili con carne, a spicy stew
an advertisement

explanation.surface: An advert for chili somehow brings in a thousand of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'commercial for spicy dish' is a chili ad, so the dish comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiliad is a group of a thousand, especially a thousand years, from the Greek for thousand.

clue.text: Tune car differently (it's a hybrid)

indicators.note: arranged differently means the letters are put in another order

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Tuning up a hybrid car in some new way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hybrid' looks like a hybrid car, but the hybrid here is half man, half horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The centaur of Greek myth combines a human torso with a horse's body, a mythical cross-breed.

clue.text: Clumsy teen love contributes to positive quality found in abundance

indicators.note: what contributes to something goes into it, so these letters are put inside another word

parts.note: an asset or advantage is a plus

indicators.note: something clumsy is awkwardly put together, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
love is zero in tennis, and zero looks like O

explanation.surface: An awkward teenage romance turns out to have a good side after all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'positive quality' is the outer word, not the definition; the definition is the last three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenteous is a literary synonym of plentiful, describing something present in large quantity.

clue.text: Canoe wrecked in sea

indicators.note: a wrecked boat is broken apart, so its letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the five letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A canoe comes to grief out on the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean is a vast body of salt water, loosely synonymous with the sea.

clue.text: Contraption to improve morals?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a gadget or mechanism
second meaning, read whimsically: to take the wickedness out of someone

explanation.walkthrough: Read as DE-VICE, the word would mean to remove vice, which would certainly improve one's morals; the question mark flags the made-up sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A device is a piece of equipment made for a purpose, a fair synonym of contraption.

clue.text: Actual island drain backs up after five

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five

indicators.note: in a down answer, backing up means reading upward, so the order of the letters flips

parts.note: Elba, Napoleon's island of exile
to drain is to exhaust or tire

explanation.surface: A real island drain that backs up, overflowing after five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs up' looks like a blocked drain, but it turns round both the island and the drain, which then follow the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Veritable means true or genuine, used to stress that a description really applies.

clue.text: Following gang, I take a stab at a life of crime

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
taken as written
to take a stab at something is to try it

explanation.surface: Someone who has fallen in with a gang decides to give criminal life a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following gang' tells you the I and the attempt come after the gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditry is the practice of robbery by outlaws, a criminal way of life.

clue.text: Impersonate Gene's buffalo

parts.note: to play a role is to be that character
Gene Wilder, the American comic actor

explanation.surface: Doing an impression of the buffalo that belongs to someone called Gene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffalo' looks like the animal, but it is the American verb meaning to baffle.
explanation.definitionFit: In US usage, to buffalo someone is to confuse or overawe them, much like bewilder.

clue.text: People who like to hang out in taverns and spew falsehoods

definitions.text: People who like to hang out in taverns

parts.note: barf is slang for vomit
untruths

explanation.surface: Pub regulars who throw up and tell fibs.
explanation.definitionFit: Barflies are habitual drinkers who spend much of their time at bars.

clue.text: Villains, for example, wearing insignia with a final change of direction

indicators.note: the wearer is inside the clothing, so the example word goes within the badge

indicators.text: with a final change of direction
indicators.note: the last letter is a compass point, and it is swapped for a different compass point

parts.note: an emblem or mark of rank
the abbreviation e.g.

explanation.surface: Cartoon villains sporting badges, perhaps, as they make a final U-turn.
explanation.walkthrough: The badge ends in E, which counts as east; swapping it for S, south, is the change of direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad egg is an idiom for a dishonest or untrustworthy person, a rogue.

clue.text: Crazy caper to swallow a bit of drink — a kind of porter

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the word encloses a letter
crazy suggests something disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word to be rearranged

indicators.note: a small bit of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of drink

explanation.surface: A wild escapade involves a quick nip, ending with mention of a type of dark beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' tempts toward the dark beer, but this porter carries bags. A redcap is the American term for a railway station porter.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a redcap is a baggage porter at a railway station, named for the red cap worn.

clue.text: Self-righteous reformer originally committed to fine

indicators.note: something committed to an institution is put inside it

parts.note: peachy is US slang for fine or excellent

indicators.note: originally points to the very first letter, the one at the origin of the word

parts.note: the first letter of reformer

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious reformer was at first devoted to doing good.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside PEACHY. 'fine' looks like a penalty but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Preachy describes someone who moralises tiresomely, displaying self-righteous zeal.

clue.text: What connects you to piano paradise on Earth

indicators.note: what connects the words is the run of letters bridging them, across the word boundaries

parts.note: read across the last letter of you, all of to and the start of piano

explanation.surface: Asking what links a listener to the piano, a musician's heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What connects you to piano' reads like a question about music, but it is the indicator plus the words that hold the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A utopia is an imagined perfect society, an ideal place to live, from Thomas More's book.

clue.text: In retrospect, angry about Western state making up a fact

indicators.note: looking back in retrospect means reading the result from the end to the start
about means around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: mad means angry
UT is the postal abbreviation for Utah

explanation.surface: Looking back, someone is cross about a Western state inventing a fact.
explanation.walkthrough: The containment happens first; only then is the whole thing read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information, a fact used as a basis for reasoning.

clue.text: One way to drive long distances: restricted, banished, will-less

indicators.note: something banished is sent away, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.words: One way to drive long distances
parts.note: an interstate is a US highway between states
R is the US film rating for restricted viewing

explanation.surface: A list of reasons a long-distance driver might be stuck, ending with lacking willpower.
explanation.walkthrough: The R is removed from INTERSTATE. 'will-less' looks like lacking willpower, but it means having made no legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dies intestate has left no valid testament disposing of their estate.

clue.text: Air Force One runs on empty, in flames

parts.note: standard abbreviation
Roman numeral one
R is the scoring abbreviation for runs
E marks empty on a fuel gauge

explanation.surface: The presidential plane flying on an empty tank, then catching fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air Force One' looks like the president's plane, but it splits into AF and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Afire is a literary adjective meaning burning, on fire.

clue.text: Lose sight of mythical creature heading to destruction

parts.note: a mischievous creature of folklore

indicators.note: the heading of a word is what comes at its front, its initial letter

parts.note: the first letter of destruction

explanation.surface: Losing track of a fabled monster as it heads off to wreak havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose sight of' reads as a phrase meaning stop seeing something; the definition is only 'Lose sight', with 'of' as the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To go blind is to lose one's eyesight entirely, an idiomatic phrasing.

clue.text: Ottawa leader resorted to panic

indicators.note: read as re-sorted, sorted again, so the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Canada's political leader, under pressure, falls back on panicking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ottawa leader' suggests Canada's prime minister, but the Ottawa (Odawa) are also an Indigenous people. 'resorted' looks like 'turned to' but is read as sorted again.
explanation.definitionFit: Pontiac was the 18th-century war chief of the Ottawa nation who led a 1763 uprising against the British.

clue.text: Organ's collection of musical pieces grew audible

indicators.note: audible means heard, so the words are taken by their sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a suite is a set of instrumental pieces played in sequence
bred means raised or grew

explanation.surface: A church organ's repertoire of music grew louder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ's collection of musical pieces' reads as a pipe organ's repertoire, but the organ is in the body; ''s' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetbread is the thymus or pancreas of a calf or lamb, eaten as offal.

clue.text: Once again hide the truth, speaking for count

indicators.note: speaking means said out loud, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: re- means once again, and to lie is to hide the truth

explanation.surface: Telling another fib, this time talking about a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a noun, a nobleman or a tally, but it is the verb, as in count on.
explanation.definitionFit: To count on someone is to depend on them, so count works as a synonym of rely.
